digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### pg_durable: Microsoft open sources in-database durable execution
URL: https://github.com/microsoft/pg_durable
PostgreSQL gets workflow orchestration baked into the database layer.
Microsoft releasing this signals enterprise validation of the "database as execution environment" pattern. This directly competes with Temporal and similar workflow engines, but with zero infrastructure overhead. Watch for adoption in financial services where transaction guarantees matter.

### Gemma 4 QAT models: Optimizing compression for mobile and laptop efficiency
URL: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/quantization-aware-training-gemma-4/
Google pushes quantization-aware training to get competitive models running on edge devices.
The mobile AI inference war is heating up. QAT represents a meaningful compression technique that maintains model quality while slashing compute requirements. This is Google playing defense against Apple's on-device strategy while enabling a new class of offline-capable applications.

### When AI builds itself
URL: https://www.anthropic.com/institute/recursive-self-improvement
Anthropic publishes research on recursive self-improvement capabilities.
This is the AI safety lab publicly documenting capability thresholds that matter for policy. The timing suggests regulatory positioning ahead of potential EU AI Act enforcement actions. Required reading for anyone modeling AI company trajectories.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### Google will pay SpaceX $920M per month for compute
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/google-will-pay-spacex-920m-per-month-for-compute/
Google outsourcing compute to SpaceX at $11B annually signals severe capacity constraints.
This is extraordinary. Google, owner of the largest private compute infrastructure on Earth, is paying a rocket company for AI capacity. The "unexpected demand" language is corporate-speak for "we dramatically underestimated consumption." Implies hyperscaler capex projections are still too conservative.

### Supabase doubles valuation to $10B in 8 months
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/supabase-doubles-valuation-to-10b-in-8-months/
Open-source Firebase alternative hits $10B on vibe-coding tailwinds.
Supabase is the canonical example of AI coding tools driving infrastructure demand. When Claude writes code, it defaults to familiar patterns—and Supabase has become the default backend. The valuation implies 20-30x ARR multiples; watch whether this holds as rate sensitivity returns.

### Reid Hoffman is leaving Microsoft's board to go 'founder mode' with startup Manus
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/reid-hoffman-is-leaving-microsofts-board-to-go-founder-mode-with-startup-manus/
LinkedIn founder exits Microsoft board to run AI drug discovery company full-time.
Board departures from big tech to run portfolio companies signal where smart money sees asymmetric returns. Manus is Hoffman's bet that AI-native drug discovery will produce venture-scale outcomes. The "founder mode" framing suggests he sees operational involvement as necessary to win.

### AirTrunk commits $30B to build 5GW of AI data centers in India
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/airtrunk-commits-30b-to-build-5gw-of-ai-data-centers-in-india/
Australian data center operator makes massive India infrastructure bet.
5GW is roughly the power consumption of a mid-sized European country. This positions India as the training and inference overflow destination for APAC. The $30B commitment size suggests AirTrunk has LOIs from hyperscalers that de-risk the build.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Did Claude increase bugs in rsync?
URL: https://alexispurslane.github.io/rsync-analysis/
Empirical analysis of AI-assisted contributions to critical open-source infrastructure.
This is the kind of rigorous post-hoc analysis the industry needs. If AI tools are introducing defects into battle-tested codebases, the productivity gains may be illusory. The rsync case study has implications for any org evaluating AI coding tool ROI.

### The token bill comes due: Inside the industry scramble to manage AI's runaway costs
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/the-token-bill-comes-due-inside-the-industry-scramble-to-manage-ais-runaway-costs/
Enterprise AI deployments hitting cost walls as token consumption explodes.
The shift from "tokenmaxxing" to guardrails mirrors every enterprise software adoption cycle. First you ship features, then you get the bill. This creates immediate opportunity for cost optimization tooling and inference efficiency plays.

### Former cyber executive turned whistleblower accuses IBM of covering up several data breaches
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/05/former-cyber-executive-turned-whistleblower-accuses-ibm-of-covering-up-several-data-breaches/
Lawsuit alleges IBM concealed multiple breaches from mid-2010s.
If substantiated, this creates material litigation risk and potential SEC disclosure violations. IBM's government contracts and regulated industry relationships make this particularly damaging. Watch for parallel investigations from state AGs.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The Google-SpaceX compute deal is the week's clearest signal: even hyperscalers are capacity-constrained, and the AI infrastructure buildout is far from over. Meanwhile, the convergence of vibe-coding backlash (rsync bugs, token cost spirals) and massive infrastructure bets ($30B India data centers, $10B Supabase) suggests we're entering the "measure twice" phase of AI adoption—where the easy wins are priced in and execution separates winners from write-downs.
